articles.body: Megastar Chiranjeevi’s praise for Jason Sanjay became one of the highlights of the Hyderabad pre-release event of 'Sigma'. Speaking as the chief guest, Chiranjeevi recalled his first meeting with the debutant filmmaker and said Jason’s appearance immediately reminded him of his father, actor-turned-politician Vijay, during his younger days.Chiranjeevi praises Jason Sanjay at 'Sigma' eventAs reported by Filmibeat, Chiranjeevi recalled meeting Jason for the first time and said his appearance took him back to the period when Vijay was still establishing himself in the film industry.“When he came to meet me, he reminded me of his father Vijay during 1993-94,” Chiranjeevi said.The veteran actor also revealed that he had asked Jason whether he wanted to pursue acting or direction. Jason, however, made his preference clear, telling Chiranjeevi that his real interest lay in writing and filmmaking.Chiranjeevi connects Jason Sanjay with Vijay’s family film legacyChiranjeevi also spoke about the filmmaking lineage Jason comes from. He pointed out that the young director has chosen a creative path closely connected to his grandparents, filmmaker S. A. Chandrasekhar and writer Shoba.“S S Chandrasekhar was a very good director, while his wife Shoba garu penned scripts. Sanjay is taking forward the skills of his grandparents. He has inherited those genes and has turned director,” he said.Chiranjeevi has previously worked with S. A. Chandrasekhar, giving him a long-standing association with Vijay’s family. His remarks therefore placed Jason’s debut within a film legacy spanning several generations, while also acknowledging the filmmaker’s decision to work behind the camera.Chiranjeevi recalls Vijay’s rise and wishes Jason success as a directorThe Megastar also recalled watching Vijay’s journey from his early years in cinema to becoming one of Tamil cinema’s leading stars. He said he hoped Jason would similarly find his own path and achieve his ambitions as a filmmaker.“I have seen his father Vijay rise to meteoric heights as an actor, and I wish Jason Sanjay also achieves his goals as a director. I think his debut film Sigma will pave the way for his dreams,” Chiranjeevi said.Jason Sanjay says Vijay is excited to watch 'Sigma' but will not promote itJason Sanjay has previously addressed his father Vijay’s involvement in the promotional campaign for Sigma. He said Vijay is looking forward to watching the film but will not actively promote it. Jason explained that Vijay’s responsibilities as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister were one reason for his absence from the promotional campaign. He also said he wanted the focus to remain on the film and its cast and crew rather than on his father’s presence.“My father is waiting for the release of Sigma. He won’t be promoting my film. I want the promotions to be about the film and not him. I don’t want it to overlap,” Jason said at a press interaction.At a recent 'Sigma' event, Jason Sanjay also acknowledged the support of his parents and sister, thanking his father Vijay, mother Sangeetha and sister Divya Saasha.'Sigma' marks Jason Sanjay’s first film as a director'Sigma', starring Sundeep Kishan and Faria Abdullah, is scheduled to release theatrically on October 2. articles.title: Here’s What Netflix’s“ Unabomber” Got Right and Wrong About the Disturbing Real-Life Events
articles.summary: The Netflix film, which premiered Sept. 25, sees Jacob Tremblay portray real-life domestic terrorist Ted Kaczynski
articles.body:
Unabomber was released on Netflix on Sept. 25

The film combines fact and fiction in its depiction of terrorist Ted Kaczynski and his crimes

The FBI did use linguistic analysis of Kaczynski's manifesto to identify him, but Shailene Woodley's character's involvement in these findings is fictional

The Netflix film Unabomber shows how Theodore "Ted" Kaczynski went from an unassuming, introverted math prodigy to a domestic terrorist who killed three people and injured more than 20 others with 16 homemade bombs over the course of 17 years.

With Jacob Tremblay portraying Kaczynski, the movie focuses largely on Kaczynski's adolescence and coming of age at Harvard University, where he participated in controversial psychological experiments led by Dr. Henry A. Murray ( Russell Crowe ) and Christiana Morgan ( Annabelle Wallis ). In the movie, the experiments were part of what eventually drove Kaczynski to become the Unabomber, a moniker that came from the FBI's code name for the case, UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing).

Kaczynski planted some of his homemade explosives and sent others to victims and targets in the mail until the FBI caught him in April 1996, ending what became one of the longest and most expensive manhunts in the agency's history, per History.com .

Below, here's what Netflix's Unabomber got right and wrong about the real-life events.

Was Ted Kaczynski really a mathematical genius?

As portrayed in the Netflix film, Kaczynski was considered a child prodigy , reportedly scoring 167 on an I.Q. test in fifth grade, per The Atlantic . He was so advanced in mathematics that he skipped sixth and 11th grades, going on to enroll at Harvard University on a scholarship at 16 years old, per The Washington Post .

Kaczynski graduated from Harvard in 1962, then earned his master's and doctoral degrees from the University of Michigan. In 1967, Kaczynski, then 25, became an assistant mathematics professor at University of California, Berkeley.

Did Ted Kaczynski really not get along with other students?

Kaczynski's brother, David, previously told PEOPLE that Kaczynski only had a few friends in high school and none in college.

In May 2012, one of Kaczynski's Harvard suitemates, Patrick S. McIntosh, told The Harvard Crimson that Kaczynski was withdrawn, never spoke to any of his classmates and ate alone in the dining hall, even when others tried to engage with him. McIntosh also recalled Kaczynski's room smelling of "piles of books and uneaten sandwiches."

Another student named John V. Federico, however, said that while Kaczynski was "on the shy side," he was "certainly friendly" when he was included in discussions.

Was Ted Kaczsynski really part of a Harvard psychology experiment?

Yes, Kaczynski really was part of a Harvard psychology experiment under Murray and Morgan.

Murray received graduate degrees in medicine and biology from Columbia University, as well as a Ph.D in biochemistry from the University of Cambridge, per his Harvard University bio . He was considered a pioneer in the field of psychoanalysis, having worked to improve the Thematic Apperception Test, or TAT, much like in the Netflix film. He also was, in real life as in the film, a scholar of Herman Melville and a fan of Moby-Dick , per The New York Times .

According to The Guardian , the experiment in which Kaczynski and 21 other undergraduates were told they'd debate another student was actually intended to measure how people react under stress. Per the outlet, the experiment resulted in the participants being subjected to what Murray described as "vehement, sweeping, and personally abusive" interrogations.

Former philosophy professor Alston Chase wrote in The Guardian that it's "clear" Murray's experiment "deeply affected at least some of its subjects." However, experts have noted that the study's actual impacts on Kaczynski's life and mental health, if any, were never proven, and could be considered "coincidental."

There is also no evidence that Kaczynski ever walked in on Murray and Morgan being intimate, though the colleagues were romantically involved, per The New York Times .

Did Henry A. Murray really work with the CIA?

It is true that Murray worked with the CIA, as was briefly depicted in Unabomber . The New York Times reported that Murray began working with the Office of Strategic Services (which would later become the CIA) in 1943 to use psychology to help select undercover agents. (Years earlier, the U.S. government had recruited him to create a psychological profile of Adolph Hitler , per his Harvard University bio.)

According to The Washington Post , some of Murray's experiments may have been part of the CIA's MKUltra program , which was inspired by the use of mind-control techniques on U.S. prisoners of war in Korea by the Soviet Union, China and North Korea.

Was Ted Kaczynski really estranged from his parents?

As briefly explained in the movie, Kaczynski became estranged from his parents, homemaker Wanda and sausage maker Theodore Richard .

David previously told PEOPLE that Kaczynski resented Theodore and Wanda and believed that they only ever valued his career and intellect and never loved him as a person. David also recalled that after their father was diagnosed with terminal cancer and died by suicide in 1990, Kaczynski didn't attend the funeral, and rather called his mother on the day of the memorial.

Did Ted Kaczynski really build his own cabin in the woods?

Kaczynski and David, who was living in a Montana apartment at the time, pooled their resources and bought 1.4 acres of land together in Lincoln, Mont., in 1971, David previously told PEOPLE.

There, Kaczynski built his cabin, which lacked electricity and running water, per The New York Times . Kaczynski lived in the cabin for more than two decades until his arrest. Federal authorities reported finding bomb-making equipment, a live bomb, a draft of an anti-technology manifesto sent to news organizations by the Unabomber and a typewriter inside the cabin, per CNN .

Did newspapers really publish the "Unabomber Manifesto"?

In 1995, Kaczynski, still known anonymously as the Unabomber at the time, sent a copy of Industrial Society and Its Future — the 35,000-word anti-tech essay that would become known as the "Unabomber Manifesto" — to both The New York Times and The Washington Post , per The National Archives Foundation .

He threatened to send a bomb to an unspecified destination "with intent to kill" unless one of the newspapers published the manuscript in full, per The Washington Post .

On Sept. 19, 1995, under advisement from the FBI and then-Attorney General Janet Reno, The Washington Post published Kaczynski's manifesto under the byline FC, which stood for "Freedom Club."

Did Ted Kaczynski really harass a woman he went on a date with?

Though it's only mentioned briefly in the Unabomber film, Kaczynski did harass a woman with whom he and David worked at a foam rubber factory in 1978.

The woman, who was a supervisor, told SFGate she and Kaczynski went on one dinner date and baked an apple pie, after which she declined to see him again because they didn't have much in common "socially." She denied their relationship ever having gotten to a romantic stage.

After she rejected him, Kaczynski began writing profane poems and messages about the woman and leaving them around the factory before he was fired by his brother.

She also emphasized that she had no idea he was the Unabomber at the time, describing Kaczynski as "quiet" and "intelligent."

Did Joanne Miller really help catch Ted Kaczynski?

In the movie, Kaczynski's ostracization at Harvard is paralleled with that of an underestimated FBI agent named Joanne Miller ( Shailene Woodley ) whose linguistic expertise leads to Kaczynski's capture.

Miller is entirely fictional. However, Woodley's character's focus on linguistics was a key component in capturing Kaczynski in real life.

FBI criminal profiler James R. Fitzgerald began working on the Unabomber case in July 1995, but it wasn't until after Kaczynski's manifesto was published that September that investigators got a clearer picture of his identity, per NPR .

Fitzgerald said that because the initial bombings had a focus on college campuses and universities, investigators pegged the Unabomber as someone who was around ages 18-23 until the manifesto's language helped them correct their course.

"I'm picking up on some unusual language characteristics, like some archaic terms like 'broad' and 'chick' to denote women," Fitzgerald told NPR. "He uses the word 'negro' to refer to African-Americans. And this is 1995, and these words were almost like Frank Sinatra language, or something you'd hear from a '50s movie or something. And right away, that helped me age the author."

Did Ted Kaczynski's brother really turn him in?

After the "Unabomber Manifesto" was published, David and his wife Linda recognized a specific phrase, "cool-headed logician," that matched letters David had from Kaczynski. "I had never heard anyone else use that phrase," David previously told PEOPLE.

They presented the letters to one of Linda's friends, who was a private investigator, who then showed the letters to a linguistics expert. The linguistics specialist told them that there was an 80% chance that the manifesto writer also wrote the letter, and David and Patrick found a way to then contact the FBI.

Did CBS really get Ted Kaczynski's name before he was arrested?

In the movie, the Unabomber's identity is leaked to CBS before they have a chance to apprehend him, putting their plan at risk until Miller strikes a deal with them: If they wait to publish his name, they can have the exclusive information that it was Kaczynski's own brother who turned him in.

In real life, though, it wasn't just Kaczynski's identity that was leaked to CBS News ahead of his arrest — David's cooperation with the FBI leaked to the media as well, despite the FBI assuring him he would stay anonymous, per Time .

According to the Los Angeles Times , CBS reported that a search was imminent on the "best suspect" in the years-long investigation. As a result, the FBI said that the broadcast forced them to move in on Kaczynski in his cabin earlier than they'd originally planned.

In the aftermath, FBI officials disagreed over whether the agency had to move prematurely with their raid because of the CBS broadcast. However, the FBI issued a statement at the time praising CBS for temporarily holding their broadcast at the FBI's request, saying that the media organization's decision allowed them to carry out the arrest with no injuries, per the Los Angeles Times .

According to The Record , Lane Venardos, who was vice president of CBS at the time, said that they had already held the story for two days at the FBI's request, only broadcasting it when they feared other networks were about to break the story instead. He said they had been in contact with a senior FBI official 15 minutes before the report was aired and that no objections were raised, adding that they wouldn't have put the investigation or the agents at any risk.

Did Ted Kaczynski really have schizophrenia?

In the movie, Murray tells Kaczynski that he believes he has schizophrenia. In real life, however, a court-appointed psychiatrist diagnosed Kaczynski with schizophrenia amid his trial, per The New York Times .

Those close to Kaczynski, including David, believed he was mentally ill for a long time, but Kaczynski insisted he was not, even trying to fire his legal team to stop them from using that argument as a defense, per Time . Some experts also rejected the claims of Kaczynski's mental illness, including forensic psychiatrist Dr. Park Dietz, who told The New Yorker in March 1998 that the results of Kaczynski's evaluation and his journals "scream geek, not schizophrenic."

Shortly after his diagnosis, Kaczynski agreed to plead guilty to avoid the death penalty in exchange for multiple life sentences without a chance of parole, per The New York Times .

Kaczynski served his sentence in a super-max prison in Florence, Colo., Time reported, but was later transferred to Federal Medical Center in North Carolina due to health issues. In March 2021, he was diagnosed with rectal cancer, per NBC News . Kaczynski died by suicide at age 81 in June 2023.

articles.summary: Princess Diana’s brother reveals surprising details about her private life, including a powerful American suitor, royal tensions and plans for a fresh start.
articles.body: Princess Diana’s younger brother, Charles Spencer, released his memoir "Swan Song," about the beloved royal this week revealing new details about the late royal’s life behind palace walls. From claims about then-Prince Charles’ treatment of Diana to an American politician who reportedly courted her after her divorce, here are some of the memoir’s biggest revelations. Charles' reaction to Diana's death Spencer wrote that on the morning Diana died, then-Prince Charles sounded "giddily elated – like a lottery winner," he remembered thinking at the time. He wrote that Charles was "strangely matter-of-fact, given the enormity of the disaster." PRINCESS DIANA'S HONEYMOON LETTER REVEALS A YOUNG BRIDE 'PLAYING WITH GROWN-UPS' IN THE ROYAL FAMILY In hindsight, Spencer wrote, he believed that Charles’ first reaction to her death was that it likely freed him up to "marry the woman he loved, rather than appreciating the loss of one he did not." He also wrote that while they were arguing over funeral arrangements, Charles told him, "Rest assured … we'll forget her soon enough!" PRINCE HARRY'S RUMORED DIANA FILM 'MIGHT FEEL LIKE ANOTHER BETRAYAL' TO PRINCE WILLIAM AS RIFT GROWS: EXPERT Spencer said he was stunned for a few seconds before responding, "I can’t believe you just said that," before hanging up. Earlier in their conversation, Spencer wrote that Charles accused the Spencer family of having no sense of duty because Spener had objected to Princes Harry and William walking behind their mother’s coffin. PRINCESS DIANA NEVER FORGAVE SARAH FERGUSON FOR ONE BETRAYAL THAT ENDED THEIR FRIENDSHIP: BOOK Spencer wrote that he believed the diatribe was the result of Charles’ "pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death." After the excerpt from the book was released last week, Buckingham Palace issued a rare statement. "While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," the statement said. Diana considered moving to South Africa with heart surgeon boyfriend Spencer wrote that after falling in love with heart surgeon Dr. Hasnat Khan following her divorce, Diana had the "naïve yet impossible" dream of moving to South Africa — where Spencer lived at the time — with her boyfriend because England had become "intolerable" to her. "Might they, she dared hope, move there together, and carve out a life?" he wrote. He said she dreamed that Khan could work at a hospital in Cape Town, and they could live "happily — normally — nearby" her brother. "The other side of the world seemed to offer the possibility of asylum," he wrote. INSIDE PRINCESS DIANA AND JFK JR.'S SECRET MEETING THAT FUELED ROMANCE RUMORS FOR DECADES One of Diana’s post-divorce suitors was an American politician Spencer said that Diana once asked him if he thought she’d make a good American first lady, explaining that one of her "many powerful aging American suitors, keen to secure her as the ultimate trophy wife, had told her he was sure to win the presidency if she married him." He said that Diana was more "titillated" by the idea of living in the White House than by the prospect of marrying the "would-be elderly husband." Diana, he said, had a "mischievous attraction to reinventing herself in a role that would make her enemies in the British Royal Family sick with jealousy, while ushering in an era of glamour in the White House that would surely have surpassed even that of the Jackie Kennedy years." Diana almost canceled the ‘Panorama’ interview Despite "Panorama" reporter Martin Bashir allegedly telling Diana a series of falsehoods, including that she was being surveilled by MI6, that Prince William was unwittingly bugging her through a device on his watch and that her children’s nanny had aborted Prince Charles' child after an affair, Diana almost canceled the interview, Spencer said. But Bashir and the show’s executive producer persisted, Spencer wrote. He said they arranged a clandestine meeting in a parking garage, where Spencer believes they persuaded Diana that her life was in "imminent" danger and that doing the interview was the best way to protect herself. Spencer depicts then-Prince Charles as resentful of his position Spencer said he had a conversation with Charles after his own father’s funeral, during which Charles told him he was "lucky" his father had died because he got to inherit when he was "so young." Charles allegedly said that while Spencer was inheriting his ancestral home of Althorp in his 20s, the prince complained that he was 43 and employed 50 people, "but my parents insist on treating me like — like a child!" Spencer said he found the claim improbable, but didn't press her for more information because he was focused on the realization that she was ending her marriage and her "dreams." She loved flowers, especially forget-me-nots, listened to the Beatles and David Bowie, and liked the soap opera "Crossroads." articles.title: Questions remain as details keep emerging in Hayden Panettiere death
articles.summary: New reports detail the drugs found at the scene of Hayden Panettiere's death as the investigation continues. Here's everything to know.
articles.body:
As more details continue to emerge in the death investigation of actress Hayden Panettiere , some questions still remain.

The "Heroes" and "Nashville" star, 36, died Aug. 16 at an apartment complex in Greenville, South Carolina , from the " toxic effects of fentanyl " and other drugs, according to a release from the Greenville County Coroner's Office. An investigative report later revealed fentanyl-laced pills and an unidentified white powder were found with the former child star when she died.

Now, as investigators reveal more details about the circumstances surrounding Panettiere's death, here's what we know and are looking out for as the investigation continues.

Hayden Panettiere's life in photos, from child actor to 'Scream' star

Hayden Panettiere is dead at 36 . Best known for her roles as Claire Bennet on "Heroes," Juliette Barnes on "Nashville" and Kirby Reed in the "Scream" horror movie franchise, Panettiere started her career with roles in the TV shows "Unhappily Ever After" and "One Life to Live." Her star power rose as she performed in "Remember the Titans," "Ally BcBeal," 2005's "Racing Stripes" and the Disney film "Ice Princess" that same year; she also sang for some of her Hollywood projects, including "Tiger Cruise" and "Nashville." Panettiere welcomed a daughter with her then-fiancé, Wladimir Klitschko, in 2014, and took a hiatus from acting after "Nashville" ended in 2018. She opened up about her personal life, including her sexuality , in a memoir, "This Is Me: A Reckoning." Scroll on for a look back at her film and TV career.

Hayden Panettiere's cause of death included 4-ANPP, methocarbamol

Panettiere died from the "toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine," according to a Greenville County Coroner's Office release. Fentanyl is a synthetic opioid drug that is used to relieve pain and is around 100 times more potent than morphine and 50 times more potent than heroin as an anesthetic, according to the Drug Enforcement Administration .

The "manner of death has been ruled accident," and no signs of trauma were discovered that would have contributed to Panettiere's death, the release added.

Hayden Panettiere death investigation reveals other drugs found with star

At the scene of her fatal overdose, authorities found a bottle of Adderall as well as blue pressed pills and a cut straw that tested positive for fentanyl inside Panettiere's makeup bag, according to the USA TODAY Network's Greenville News , which obtained the investigative report from the Greenville County Medical Examiner.

Other prescription bottles were also found on the kitchen table, and glass vials and prefilled and empty syringes were found in a small lunchbox inside the refrigerator, the report said.

The investigative report also shared that unidentified white powder in a small, clear plastic bag was found inside a sunglasses case packed in the actress' suitcase. It was not immediately clear whether the white powder found in her suitcase was tested or identified, the report added.

Hayden Panettiere death investigation reveals drugs found with star: Report

What Brian Hickerson told investigators on the scene after Hayden Panettiere's death

Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother, Zach Hickerson , were on the scene and called 911 when the actress went into cardiac arrest. Now, investigators are revealing what Hickerson told them after her fatal overdose.

Brian Hickerson told investigators that the couple had arrived in South Carolina the night before, according to the Greenville County investigative report obtained by Greenville News .

In the morning, Panettiere woke up and put on makeup, he said, and the pair ate cereal together before he fell back asleep. Brian Hickerson said he woke up in the afternoon to Zach Hickerson knocking on his door so the trio could go to lunch, but upon going to wake up Panettiere, they found her "crisscross applesauce," face down and unresponsive on a sofa bed.

Brian Hickerson said he administered multiple cans of Narcan, a nasal spray that can reverse life-threatening opioid overdoses, but nothing changed. He told his brother to call 911, and they started CPR until emergency personnel arrived.

One of the brothers told the deputy that Panettiere had a long history of drug, alcohol and nitrous oxide abuse.

The report also said that a redacted name, assumed to be Brian Hickerson, was not aware of Panettiere using any illegal substances that day or the day prior, but said that she was very good at hiding them and that he had administered Narcan to her before.

Hayden Panettiere's boyfriend detained, his brother arrested

On Sept. 12, nearly a month after the "Remember the Titans" actress' death, her boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, was briefly detained by police following a reported assault at Wild Wing Café in Greenville, South Carolina. The 38-year-old was among the "multiple patrons" detained in the alleged altercation but was later released at the scene with no charges.

Police also arrested his brother Zach Hickerson – who was reportedly "highly intoxicated" and "began yelling profanities in a public setting" – and later booked him into the Greenville County Detention Center. He was released the following day after paying a $150 fine on Sept. 23, court records reviewed by USA TODAY Sept. 24 showed.

Zach Hickerson's case has since been disposed of.

Brother of Hayden Panettiere's boyfriend resolves court case after arrest

Investigators continue to investigate source of fentanyl-laced pills

Questions still remain about the source of the fentanyl-laced pills.

Investigators with the DEA and other departments, from both Los Angeles and South Carolina , are focused on identifying what drugs contributed to her death and where those drugs came from, according to ABC News , citing unnamed sources.

The department has not commented on the state of the investigation, simply noting it is "active" and telling Greenville, South Carolina, station WYFF4 that "these cases are complex and take time to develop."

Contributing: Terry Benjamin II, Greenville News; Brendan Morrow, Sameen Chaudhry, KiMi Robinson, USA TODAY

articles.title: In 2014, Akon launched a solar initiative to bring electricity to rural Africa; within a year, it reached 14 countries
articles.summary: Long before solar energy became a major part of conversations around Africa’s development, Akon was trying to tackle one of the continent’s most basic
articles.body: Long before solar energy became a major part of conversations around Africa’s development, Akon was trying to tackle one of the continent’s most basic challenges: access to electricity.In February 2014, the Senegalese-American singer launched Akon Lighting Africa, an initiative focused on using solar power to provide electricity to communities that were not connected to reliable power networks. The project was founded by Akon along with Thione Niang and Malian entrepreneur Samba Bathily.The idea was ambitious from the beginning. The initiative initially set out to bring electricity to one million African households by the end of 2014, with a particular focus on rural communities. Its approach involved solar equipment for homes as well as public infrastructure, rather than relying solely on conventional electricity grids.Why Akon wanted to focus on electricityFor Akon, the project was connected to his own childhood experience in Senegal. He and co-founder Thione Niang grew up in Kaolack, a town where access to electricity was limited. The initiative’s official account says those experiences of growing up without reliable power helped shape their decision to make energy access a priority. The reasoning behind the project went beyond simply putting lights in homes. Lack of electricity affects education, healthcare and economic activity.Solar power became the answerInstead of waiting for conventional electricity infrastructure to reach remote communities, Akon Lighting Africa promoted off-grid solar solutions.The programme worked through partnerships involving governments, businesses and organisations connected to the project. Its solutions included solar streetlights, household solar kits, community systems and solar-powered equipment.The model was also designed around financing. A 2015 statement from the initiative said solar systems were pre-financed so that equipment could be deployed more quickly, while governments and other partners participated in the wider process.From a 2014 launch to 14 countriesBy August 2014, only months after the initiative was launched, a report from Northwestern University’s Medill News Service said Akon had stated that solar installations had already reached 14 African nations. At that point, the project had completed about a quarter of its stated one-million-household target, according to the report.The initiative’s own subsequent overview similarly says that in less than one year, solar solutions including streetlights and domestic and individual kits had been installed in 14 African countries.Those countries included Mali, Senegal, Niger, Guinea, Burkina Faso, Sierra Leone, Benin, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, the Republic of Congo, Namibia, Madagascar, Kenya and Nigeria.The rapid expansion was not limited to individual houses. According to the initiative, projects reached villages, community buildings, schools and health centres, with some rural communities receiving electricity for the first time.More than streetlightsThe programme was built around the idea that electricity could change how communities function after sunset.Solar streetlights could illuminate roads and public spaces, while household systems could provide lighting and allow residents to charge phones and use basic electrical devices. The initiative also highlighted employment opportunities created through the installation and maintenance of solar equipment, particularly for young people.The project’s focus later expanded to training as well. Akon Lighting Africa and its partners developed the Solektra Solar Academy in Bamako, Mali, aimed at training young Africans in solar technology, including installation and maintenance.The bigger ambitionReaching 14 countries was presented as an early stage rather than the end goal.A 2015 United Nations Sustainable Energy for All forum document said the initiative had already reached 11 countries at that point and was seeking to accelerate rural electrification threw off-grid solar solutions.The project’s longer-term plans were considerably larger. Its stated ambition was to expand across more African countries and address energy access on a continental scale. Later project material lists 25 countries where it had projects or planned phases.The initiative also attracted attention from international organisations. In May 2015, its founders were invited to the United Nations and World Bank-backed Sustainable Energy for All Forum, where the project was presented as an example of a market-based approach to expanding energy access.Akon’s project therefore became notable not simply because a major music star entered the energy sector, but because of how quickly the initiative attempted to move from an announced goal to physical solar installations across multiple African countries. Launched in February 2014 with a target of bringing electricity to one million households, Akon Lighting Africa had reached 14 countries in less than a year, according to the project’s own account and contemporary reporting. Its work combined solar technology, public-private partnerships and local employment with a much larger objective: finding practical alternatives for communities that conventional electricity infrastructure had not yet reached.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: BROADCAST BIAS: Media bash Sydney Sweeney, but cover for leftist Macklemore
articles.summary: Sydney Sweeney's Novig sports betting ad drew more negative broadcast coverage than rapper Macklemore's antisemitic remarks, which was typical for how the media handle celebrities.
articles.body: The broadcast networks can easily demonstrate their leftist bias in the way they cover entertainers. Those who use their fame for "good" are praised, and those who are the opposite – who lean Republican – are "controversial." Nowhere was that more evident than how the press freaked out about actress Sydney Sweeney vs. how they covered for antisemitic rapper Macklemore. Sweeney, who identified as a registered Republican, keeps ending up on the "wrong" side of the networks. Last year, she made a provocative ad for blue jeans, making a pun with the word "good genes." ABC News warned: "The play on words is being compared to Nazi propaganda with racial undertones," and then invoked professor Robin Landa proclaiming the pun was racist: "The American Eugenics Movement and its prime between 1900 and 1940 weaponized the idea of good genes just to justify white supremacism." Right now, Sweeney is featured in mostly naked advertisements for a sports prediction market called Novig. articles.title: Muere Eduardo Rodríguez Rodway, último miembro fundador de Triana, a los 81 años
articles.standfirst: El último del trío original de una banda que marcó una época en la música española
articles.summary: El último del trío original de una banda que marcó una época en la música española
articles.body: El rock andaluz pierde a una de sus figuras más emblemáticas. Eduardo Rodríguez Rodway, guitarrista y miembro fundador de Triana, ha muerto este sábado a los 81 años en el Hospital Universitario de Puerto Real (Cádiz), según ha comunicado su familia. Con su desaparición se va también el último integrante de la formación original de una banda que marcó una época en la música española. La familia confirmó la noticia a través de las redes sociales con un mensaje en el que agradeció las numerosas muestras de cariño recibidas tanto durante su trayectoria artística como en estos momentos de duelo. Rodríguez Rodway fundó Triana en 1974 junto a Jesús de la Rosa y Juan José Palacios, 'Tele'. Juntos dieron forma a un sonido único que mezclaba rock progresivo, flamenco y raíces andaluzas, una fórmula que terminó convirtiéndose en la seña de identidad del llamado rock andaluz y que llevó al grupo a ocupar un lugar privilegiado en la historia de la música española. Entre 1975 y 1983, Triana publicó seis discos que dejaron una huella imborrable. Desde El Patio, considerado una obra fundamental del género, hasta Llegó el día, la banda firmó canciones que siguen formando parte de la memoria colectiva de varias generaciones. Temas como Abre la puerta, En el lago, Rumor, Tu frialdad o Una noche de amor desesperada consolidaron a la formación sevillana como uno de los grupos más influyentes del panorama nacional. La historia de Triana estuvo marcada por la tragedia. Jesús de la Rosa falleció en un accidente de tráfico en 1983, mientras que Juan José Palacios, 'Tele', murió en 2002. Desde entonces, Eduardo Rodríguez Rodway se convirtió en el único superviviente de aquel trío que revolucionó la música española durante la Transición. Lejos de desligarse de su pasado, el guitarrista mantuvo siempre vivo el legado de Triana. Continuó vinculado a la música, desarrolló proyectos propios y participó activamente en iniciativas destinadas a preservar la memoria de una banda que sigue siendo referencia para músicos y aficionados. Con la marcha de Rodríguez Rodway desaparece el último testigo directo de la formación original de Triana, un grupo cuya influencia continúa resonando más de medio siglo después de su nacimiento.

articles.title: At 7, Elias Phoenix charmed audiences as a piano prodigy on The Ellen DeGeneres Show; at 20, he opens up about alleged abuse by his mother and twin brother, suicidal thoughts and his troubled childhood
articles.summary: Trigger warning: This story discusses alleged childhood abuse, emotional and physical abuse, and suicidal thoughts.
articles.body: Trigger warning: This story discusses alleged childhood abuse, emotional and physical abuse, and suicidal thoughts.Elias Phoenix, the former child piano prodigy who became known after appearing on The Ellen DeGeneres Show at age 7, has opened up about his troubled childhood and the alleged emotional and physical abuse he says he experienced at the hands of his mother and twin brother, Zion. In an extensive interview with PEOPLE, Phoenix, now 20, spoke about his childhood fame, the pressure he experienced at home and the years-long process of coming to terms with his past.After nearly a decade away from the spotlight, Phoenix recently shared a series of videos and posts on X detailing what he describes as years of abuse within his family.“I’m finally Elias Phoenix,” he told the publication. “And I will always continue to be Elias Phoenix.”Elias Phoenix rose to fame as a child piano prodigyPhoenix was just 7 when his extraordinary piano talent brought him national attention. He had already performed twice at Carnegie Hall and earned second place at the American Protégé International Music Talent Competition.His growing recognition led to an appearance on The Ellen DeGeneres Show in 2014, where his cheerful personality and musical ability made him a memorable young guest.Looking back, Phoenix says those television appearances represented a period when he could truly be himself.The performances were “amazing,” he recalled, describing them as “almost an escape, a way I could actually be me, energetic, happy, and unburdened.”Phoenix said his enthusiasm during the show was completely genuine.“When I went out there, no one told me to act excited and overjoyed — I just naturally did from being so excited and overjoyed,” he said.He also remembered DeGeneres warmly, describing her as “the kindest and most genuine celebrity” he had met and recalling that she continued speaking with him after filming ended.Phoenix alleges he suffered abuse at homeBehind his public image as a happy and gifted young performer, however, Phoenix says his home life was vastly different.He alleges that his mother and brother repeatedly subjected him to emotional and physical abuse during his childhood. Videos he recently shared online appear to show his mother shouting at him while he was recording an audition for the Juilliard School.Phoenix has described his family's alleged treatment of him as “torture” and wrote in one social media post that it was a “miracle” he was still alive.He also alleges that his mother and brother repeatedly made comments about his weight and called him fat. According to Phoenix, the experience contributed to an eating disorder that he says has continued to affect him into adulthood.He further alleges that his mother physically assaulted him and describes discovering an email exchange between his mother and brother that he says reinforced how negatively they viewed him.The allegations have not been independently established in the material provided. Zion has not responded to multiple requests for comment from the publication.'It freed me': How his mother's death changed Phoenix's perspectivePhoenix says he began confronting his childhood experiences after his mother died in 2020, when he was still a teenager.He told the publication that her death gave him the opportunity to process emotions he had previously been unable to confront.“It freed me,” he said. “I was finally able to process everything that happened.”Phoenix says he has struggled with severe emotional distress in the years since his childhood experiences. He said he experienced suicidal thoughts over the past three years and only recently began feeling that he was moving toward a healthier place.“The lingering effects are still kicking my ass,” he said. “I have zero self-love from this.”Phoenix's relationship with his twin brotherPhoenix's relationship with his twin brother, Zion, remains complicated.According to Phoenix, the brothers reconnected through email in 2023 after several years apart and met again in person in 2025. He says the reunion ended badly and that he subsequently spent three days receiving psychiatric care while attempting to process what he says his brother had done to him.Phoenix now says he does not want further contact with Zion.“There is a ‘hurt people hurt people’ cycle I have spent my whole life trying with all my strength to avoid,” he said. “I don’t want anything to do with him anymore.”He added that he hopes his brother will eventually recognise the impact of his alleged actions and seek healing.Zion has not responded to requests for comment.Why Elias Phoenix decided to speak publiclyPhoenix says revisiting the videos of his childhood abuse was deeply unsettling because he had forgotten many of the specific incidents.“This almost feels like it was a different life,” he said, explaining that hearing his mother's voice in the recordings brought back the fear he experienced as a child.Despite the difficulty of revisiting those memories, Phoenix says he decided to share them publicly because he wanted to tell his story and offer reassurance to others experiencing abuse.“Just because someone is your mom doesn’t mean they get a pass to abuse you and ruin your life,” he said. “You don’t owe them your forgiveness. Sometimes, biological family isn’t your real family, and that’s not your fault.”From child star to reclaiming his identityPhoenix says the public response to his revelations has been unexpectedly meaningful.For years, he says, the public primarily knew him as the cheerful child piano prodigy who appeared on television. Now, he feels people are seeing a much more complicated version of his life.“My public self has always been the child piano prodigy on TV shows,” he said. “But this depressed, abused, imperfect, anorexic and sad Elias has been given more public love in just a couple days than I ever previously had from the me I was forcing myself to be.”Disclaimer: The allegations of abuse are based on Elias Phoenix’s account and have not been independently verified. articles.title: 'Primetime' Review: Robert Pattinson channels Chris Hansen in riveting dramatization of 'To Catch a Predator'
articles.summary: Fox News Digital reviews A24's new reality TV thriller "Primetime" starring Robert Pattison, Merritt Wever and Skyler Gisondo. Directed by Lance Oppenheim.
articles.body: "Have a seat." Those words were memorably said by Chris Hansen, the "Dateline NBC" correspondent who hosted the provocative reality series "To Catch a Predator" during the 2000s. Hansen, notably, had zero involvement in the making of A24's new film, "Primetime," which was adapted from a 2007 Esquire article titled "Tonight on Dateline This Man Will Die." In fact, according to Hansen, the studio wanted him to sign a restrictive agreement before showing him the movie, which he refused to do. After watching "Primetime," you can see why A24 was hoping for a legal cover. Because unless you're Hansen or any other key people involved, it's difficult to know where the reality ends and where the fiction begins. ‘RESIDENT EVIL’ REVIEW: DIRECTOR ZACH CREGGER DELIVERS INFECTIOUS REBOOT TO GORY VIDEO GAME FRANCHISE Robert Pattinson steps into the role as Hansen, a self-aggrandizing and rather eccentric journalist eying to be taken seriously by his NBC colleagues — perhaps with the success of "To Catch a Predator." If you aren't familiar, "To Catch a Predator" exposed men who believed they were meeting minors after sexually explicit online conversations. Instead, they walked into sting operations that typically ended with Hansen emerging from another room to confront them before police made arrests. The show's producer, Andie Bender (Merritt Wever) is just as essential as its star. Her job is to keep the engine running and to make sure Hansen doesn't drift into a mental abyss. It isn't until she and Hansen are brought into the office of NBC chief Jeff Zucker (humorously played by Zucker himself), who informs them he's moving their show into primetime, giving them the daunting task of going up against ABC juggernaut "LOST" in the same time slot. 'THE DOG STARS' REVIEW: JACOB ELORDI FIGHTS FOR SURVIVAL IN RIDLEY SCOTT'S DULL POST-APOCALYPTIC WESTERN In "Primetime," the predators are also the prey as Hansen and his team go to incredible lengths to nab a creep, but more importantly, to make great television. Some members of the team grapple with the ethics and morality of their line of work. Hansen, at least the film's version of him, views himself as a saint, carrying out a righteous mission despite his own shortcomings in his personal life. But it's far more nuanced for new hire Dan Plumb (Skyler Gisondo), a 23-year-old aspiring actor hired to play a 13-year-old decoy. You can tell how visibly shaken he is by the process, and he struggles with whether obtaining the coveted Screen Actors Guild membership card is worth ruining other people's lives for. BOX OFFICE COMEBACK: HOW SUMMER 2026 OFFERS A GLIMMER OF HOPE FOR HOLLYWOOD IN THE POST-COVID ERA Pattinson has had an impressive year between "The Drama" and "The Odyssey" (not to mention "Dune: Part Three" in December), proving he's come a long way from his "Twilight" days. He gives a career-best performance as a self-obsessed, borderline unhinged NBC host. While he gets top billing, the emotional crutch of the entire movie rests on Gisondo's shoulders. Best known for his stint on HBO's "The Righteous Gemstones" and more recently playing Jimmy Olsen in the new "Superman" movie, Gisondo is able to show depth from Dan's charming naivety to utter demoralization. Wever also shines as the no-nonsense producer who has to put up with a lot of nonsense. Director Lance Oppenheim's background in documentaries shows in "Primetime" between the reliance on the hidden cameras that only fuels the intensity and the cutaways to various cultural references. The low-resolution style takes viewers back to a pre-4K era and the shadows provide a noir element. CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS The Verdict What can be viewed as an indictment of how sleazy the television industry can be, "Primetime" isn't exactly the feel-good movie of the year, but it's a riveting thriller that showcases outstanding performances from Pattinson, Gisondo and Wever. ★★★ ½ — SEE IT NOW "Primetime" is rated R for disturbing sexual material, graphic nudity, some violent content, and language. articles.body: The much-awaited ‘Ramayana’, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, has been generating buzz ever since its cast was announced. One casting choice that has drawn particular attention is Yash stepping into the role of Ravana. At a recent promotional event for the film, which saw YouTuber MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson) in attendance, producer Namit Malhotra opened up about what made the casting decision so significant, along with the actor’s contribution to the ambitious project.Namit Malhotra on what Ravana symbolizesMalhotra said, “Ravana symbolizes that force, that energy, that aspect in all of us that resides in our consciousness when we get overtaken by greed, power and the ability to control everything; we lose the goodness, the compassion and the ability to sacrifice. Ravana represented that energy. All of us should always remember that whenever we are on the path to achieving great things, we must never forget where we came from. And that’s one mistake that Ravana made, which brought his downfall, when he had all the power, all the strength in the world.”Namit Malhotra calls Yash a ‘pillar of support’Talking about Yash, Malhotra stated, “Yash could not make it [to the event]. He is absolutely a superstar playing the role of Ravana. One of the things that I must state is that when this film had to be made, I needed someone like him to really have the ability to stand there and become this pillar of support.”Malhotra further spoke about the difficulty of essaying Ravana, a character with deep roots in Indian mythology.“Because to play Ravana, who is so disliked, it took someone like him to have the courage to come on board as a producer and really support our aspiration of making ‘Ramayana’ not just to make every Indian proud, but also to take it to the entire world. And that’s what we’re doing. We miss you, Yash. I hope you’re feeling better, but this journey would not be complete without you.”Namit Malhotra reveals collaboration with MrBeast on ‘Angry Birds 3’At the event, Malhotra also opened up about teaming up with MrBeast for a separate project.“And for all of you who also, you know, may not know, in fact, I just spoke with MrBeast. articles.title: 'Mike & Molly' star Billy Gardell admits weight loss surgery 'probably saved' his life
articles.summary: Billy Gardell says bariatric surgery "probably saved my life" after type 2 diabetes and heart concerns forced him to make a drastic decision.
articles.body: "Mike & Molly" star Billy Gardell is sharing how his dramatic weight loss following his bariatric surgery in 2021 has changed his life. During a recent appearance on the "Breaking Bread" podcast, the 57-year-old actor said his decision to undergo the surgery "probably saved my life" and described the circumstances which led to him deciding that was the right route for him. He explained that he had developed type 2 diabetes, as well as "some cholesterol stuff, some heart stuff," joking that his doctor told him that "after 50 the warranties start running out." "You can't outrun those. I think the only reason I was able to survive as long as I did is one, I got decent genetics, and two was I played some sports when I was younger. So I was a big fat guy, but I was a pretty solid fat guy, and I could carry the weight for a long time, but eventually you can't outrun that." 'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE SAYS ONE HARD TRUTH FUELED HIS 300-POUND WEIGHT LOSS After a certain point, Gardell said his doctor approached him and said, "You have to do something." "I got to the point where I hurt my knee and I couldn't even walk for exercise, and I was like, I have to do something drastic," he said. "So I got the surgery, and it's been a couple years now and I probably saved my life. I'm not on any medication. Diabetes is gone." Five years after the surgery, the actor explained he has "to be real selective" about what he eats, because he only has "12 ounces to work with," but said the issue with that is "the fat Hulk is still running around" in his mind wanting to overindulge. Aside from saving his life, the surgery and resulting weight loss also allowed him to do things he couldn't do before, including hiking with his wife and buying something "off the rack" when shopping at the mall. Gardell explained he decided to get healthy not only for himself, but also for his wife, Patty Knight and their son, William, calling them "my motivating factors." "It was like I don't want to survive what I've survived, succeed where I succeeded, and then not be able to get out of a chair. So I had to look that in its face. And for anybody out there struggling, if I can do it, you can do it. And don't let nobody tell you different. Do whatever it takes." articles.body:
Juventus Women began their 2026/27 Serie A Women campaign with a victory. The Bianconere came from behind to beat Napoli Women 3-1 in Biella , with Alba Redondo , Emma Stølen Godø and Chiba all finding the net.

Here are the key facts and figures from the match.

WINNING START | Juventus have won nine of their 10 opening matches of a Serie A season, drawing the other, since making their debut in the competition in 2017/18. Across those matches, the Bianconere have scored 34 goals and conceded just seven.

COMEBACK | Juventus won a Serie A match after conceding the opening goal for the first time since December 2025. On that occasion, the opponents were also Napoli, with the Bianconere coming from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

DOUBLE FIGURES | Napoli are the sixth side against whom Juventus have recorded at least 10 Serie A victories, after Fiorentina (17), Sassuolo (15), Roma (13), Inter and Milan (11). The Bianconere now have 10 wins and one draw from 11 top-flight meetings with Napoli.

REDONDO | Alba Redondo is only the second foreign player to score Juventus' first Serie A goal of a season, after Amanda Nildén did so against Pomigliano in 2023/24.

ALBA AGAIN | Redondo scored on her first appearance of the season in one of Europe's top five leagues for the first time since September 2023, when she found the net for Levante in the Spanish Primera División.

GODØ | Napoli are the third side against whom Emma Stølen Godø has scored more than once for Juventus across all competitions, after Parma and Fiorentina, against whom she has scored twice.

IMPACT OFF THE BENCH | Since the start of last season, no Serie A side have had more different substitutes score than Juventus: six, level with Inter. Over the same period, only Inter have scored more goals through substitutes (nine) than the Bianconere (seven, level with Roma).

HEAD-TO-HEAD | Among the teams Napoli have never beaten in Serie A, only against Milan have they played more matches (12: four draws and eight defeats) than against Juventus (11: one draw and 10 defeats). The Bianconere are also the first side against whom Napoli have suffered at least 10 defeats in the Italian top flight.
